newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CSL sees lower year growth than half.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CSL sees lower year growth than half.

text.p: Vaccine and blood products manufacturer CSL Ltd said on Wednesday that full-year growth would be lower than that achieved in the first half.

"Indications are that although growth in after-tax profit will continue, the annual rate of growth will be lower than that achieved in the first half," managing director Brian McNamee said in a statement.
CSL earlier anounced a 35 percent rise in net profit for the six months to December 31, 1996 to $12.45 million.
McNamee said U.S. sales were affected by particularly competitive trading conditions, but parent sales rose 5 percent to take group sales to A$131.5 million.
"Consistent with our strategy, we have achieved growth in sales of higher margin productions to produce a sold EBIT for the half," McNamee said.

McNamee said CSL had also joined the top 10 Australian corporations ranked by total expenditure on research and development, and remained the largest investor in the Australian pharmaceutical industry in 1994-95, according to a recent survey.
CSL shares were 21 cents higher at A$6.00 at 12.20 p.m. (0120 GMT).
